subject: english-literature
title: Streams and Echoes
welcome_lead: Sometimes the voice flows like a river of thought.
meta_desc: KS3 English Literature adventure on stream of consciousness and voice effects.
final_note: You can now recognise stream of consciousness and voice effects.

concepts.def: Continuous flow of thoughts on page.
Distinct narrator style on the page.

walkthroughs.body_html: Stream of consciousness writes thoughts as they tumble — fragmented, jumping. Virginia Woolf and James Joyce are famous for it.
Tone = how the voice feels (warm, sneering, anxious). Register = formality (formal/informal). Both shape voice.
Dialogue reveals character. The narrator may sound different from the characters — distinct voice at every level.

mcqs.q: Fragmented thoughts tumbling across the page is.

numericals.q: How many voice terms here (stream, interior, tone, register, dialogue, voice)?

free_texts.q: A character thinking on the page is interior ____.
